description_full: Masco Corporation provides home improvement and building products in North America, Europe, and internationally. The company's Plumbing Products segment offers faucets, showerheads, handheld showers, valves, bath hardware and accessories, bathing units, shower bases and enclosures, shower drains, steam shower systems, water filtration systems, and sinks and kitchen accessories; acrylic tubs, bath and shower enclosures, and shower bases and trays; spas, exercise pools, and aquatic fitness systems and saunas; brass, copper, and composite plumbing system component and other non-decorative plumbing products; water products; and thermoplastic products, extruded plastic profiles, and specialized fabrication products, as well as PEX tubing products. This segment provides its products under the DELTA, BRIZO, PEERLESS, HANSGROHE, AXOR, KRAUS, NEWPORT BRASS, GINGER, WALTEC, BRISTAN, HERITAGE, MIROLIN, HOT SPRING, CALDERA, FREEFLOW SPAS, FANTASY SPAS, AQUATERRA, LIFESMART, ENDLESS POOLS, TYLO, FINNLEO, HELO, BRASSCRAFT, PLUMBSHOP, and MASTER PLUMBER brands, as well as under private label to home center and online retailers, mass merchandisers, wholesalers and distributors, plumbers, building contractors, remodelers, smaller retailers, and consumers and homebuilders. Its Decorative Architectural Products segment offers paints, primers, specialty coatings, stains, and waterproofing products, as well as paint applicators and accessories; cabinet and door hardware, functional hardware, hook and hook rail products, and outdoor living hardware; and decorative bath hardware, shower accessories, and shower doors. This segment provides its products under the BEHR, KILZ, WHIZZ, LIBERTY, and FRANKLIN BRASS brands to home center and other retailers, mass and online retailers, other specialty retailers, and original equipment manufacturers and wholesalers. The company was incorporated in 1929 and is headquartered in Livonia, Michigan.

financial_summary: Masco Corporation is a large-cap industrials business with a $15.8B market cap on $7.6B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -4% over the past three years and +1% annually across the full decade, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome.
Returns on capital run at 50% against a 9% cost of capital — a 41-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, with gross margins sitting at 32%.

The business throws off $866M in free cash flow — roughly 11 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.26× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.6× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage of 12× is fortress-like.

Management returns a meaningful 5.2% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.

sect: Its 17% operating margin runs 8pp above the Industrials median (9%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
Its share of sector profits slightly exceeds its share of revenue (1.50x).

Over five years it has been losing share of the sector profit pool (-11.6% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.01 across 544 companies in the universe; the top four hold 9% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares have drifted higher, up 15% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits near the top of its 52-week range, 6% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 36% and a beta of 0.99, it moves roughly with the market.
Liquidity is deep, with about $147.4M traded a day.
In past sell-offs it fell 45% in the 2020 crash, 38% in the 2022 bear market and 83% in 2008.
val: The stock trades only 13% below its DCF fair value of $94.06, a thin margin of safety.
The fair-value models corroborate one another (dispersion 11%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $72.66 to $124 (P10-P90).
On multiples it looks cheap against Industrials peers: P/E 17.8 vs 23.3 (sector median).
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 73% above its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are mixed: an FCF yield of 5.5% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 6.5% (vs the 8% bar).
The 19 covering analysts target $82.74 on average, 1% above the price.
prof: ROIC of 50% clears the cost of capital of 8.8% by 41pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.70).
It runs a 32% gross margin and converts 11% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 1.26x.
It spends 0.4% of revenue on stock compensation.
hlth: Leverage is moderate at 1.6x net debt to EBITDA ($647.0M of cash against $2.9B of debt), above the 1.5x gate, with interest covered 12.4x.
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 4.2, in the safe zone).
growth: Revenue has compounded at -4.5% over 3 years, 1.0% over 5 years and 0.6% over 10 years, so growth is decelerating.
At current returns, reinvesting 11% of profits supports about 5.5% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Free cash flow has compounded 0.6% a year over five years, short of the 5% durability bar.
Capex roughly matches depreciation (1.1x, 2.1% of sales), a maintenance pace.
Its Rule of 40 score is 12, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
It has beaten earnings estimates by 15.8% on average.
own: Insiders hold little stock (0.2%), and reported institutional holdings exceed 100% of shares (a sign of heavy share lending).
It returns 5.2% a year to shareholders (3.6% in buybacks and 1.6% in dividends).
The share count has shrunk 4.4% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
It has paid a dividend for 42 consecutive years, raising it 12.5% a year over the last five.
people: With about 18,000 employees, each generates about $420K of revenue, in line with the Industrials median.
That works out to $48K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $2.1M (5x revenue per employee).
